newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile forestry exports fall 24 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Chile forestry exports fall 24 percent in 1996.

text.p: Chilean forestry exports fell to $1.8 billion last year, down 24 percent on 1995, mainly as a result of lower world prices for top export wood-pulp, said state forestry agency Conaf.

"These figures are explained by a general fall in the prices of forestry products," said Conaf director Jose Antonio Prado in a statement. "1995 was an exceptionally good year in terms of the price of wood-pulp, Chile's main forestry product."
Forestry products accounted for 12 percent of Chile's total exports last year against 15 percent in 1995, he said.
Output of products associated with wood-pulp fell last year with exports of wood used for pulp down 60 percent and chemical pulp shipments down 40 percent.
Exports of value-added goods including doors and window frames climbed 65 percent compared with 1995.
